instructions: koi builds and runs code from pull requests that may be hostile, exposes the result on the public internet, and holds reviewers' provider API keys in the egress proxy's memory. Review every change with that threat model in mind. Read .greptile/rules.md and docs/design.md before reviewing. Prefer a few findings that would cause a security hole, a leaked key, a lost preview, a stuck box, or records, containers and Caddy routes disagreeing over many stylistic ones.

rules.rule: Any command that includes a preview name, branch, hostname, path, or other caller-supplied value must pass it as a separate argv element (Bun.spawn or execFile with an array), never by string interpolation into a shell command. Flag template literals that build shell strings.

Preview containers must be attached only to the isolated preview network whose sole route out is the koi egress proxy. Flag any container start that uses the default bridge, host networking, extra networks, port publishing other than through Caddy, or that mounts the Docker socket or host paths.

Reviewer-provided provider keys may exist only in the browser and in the key proxy's memory. Flag code that writes them to disk, logs, environment files, container env, preview records, or any response body. Logging must redact anything that looks like a key or the koi token.

IAM policies must name specific actions and resources, scoped by ARN or the koi resource tag. Flag Action or Resource set to "*" unless a comment says the action has no resource-level scoping, and flag any role or user given permissions beyond what the component uses. There is deliberately no deploy user; flag one being added.

The instance security group may allow inbound traffic only on port 443, and only from the CloudFront origin-facing managed prefix list. The CLI reaches the box through SSM and S3, never SSH, and certificates come by DNS-01, so no other inbound rule is needed. Flag any other inbound rule.

Every hostname label the daemon, Caddy config, or Lambda accepts must be validated against the label regex in packages/shared before use. Flag Caddy site blocks or routing that would answer for a host outside *.<domain>, the configured preview domain (var.domain in infra, KOI_DOMAIN on the box).

Running koi up twice for the same name must replace the preview and keep the hostname. Daemon operations must be safe to retry after a crash mid-way (partial builds, half-started containers, stale records). Flag code paths that would leave a record and a container disagreeing.
JSON that crosses a boundary (CLI to daemon, Lambda to SSM, recipe files, preview records on disk) must be parsed with the zod schemas in packages/shared, not cast. Flag `as` casts on parsed input.
New behavior needs a bun test that fails without it. Tests may stub the AWS SDK and Docker, but must not stub the function under test. Flag changed logic without a test.
GitHub Actions must be pinned to a full commit SHA with the version in a comment.

The egress proxy addon (host/egress/koi_egress.py) may hold reviewer keys and koi tokens only in process memory. Flag any write of a key or token to disk, a log line (including warnings and exceptions), a flow dump (-w), a response body, or an error message. Every tunnel is intercepted so its TLS server name and each request's Host can be checked against the CONNECT host: flag any path that relays a tunnel unchecked (tls_clienthello ignore_connection, raw TCP, ignore_hosts). Swapping tokens for keys must stay limited to the PROVIDERS hosts.

Egress is an allowlist: only hosts in allow.txt or PROVIDERS, only on 443 (CONNECT) or 80 (plain HTTP). Flag anything that widens it implicitly: wildcard suffixes broader than one organisation's domain, IP literals, other ports, or a fallback that forwards unknown hosts.

The keys page (packages/daemon/src/keys.ts) runs on keys.<domain>, a different origin from every preview. Its API must refuse requests whose Origin is not its own, must validate tokens and keys with the shared schemas, and must never echo submitted values or proxy error text back. Its pages keep a strict CSP with no inline script and frame-ancestors 'none'. Flag any change that relaxes these.

Files a preview container needs (the CA bundle) are placed with docker create + docker cp + docker start. Flag any bind mount, volume mount, or --mount of a host path into a preview or build container.

koid's locks are taken in this order, outermost first: buildQueue (per label), builds (global semaphore), lifecycle (per label), routing (global), store mutex (per label, innermost). Flag code that takes them in another order, holds lifecycle or routing across a build, or mutates a preview record outside the store's update/upsert.

A preview container may be stopped or removed only after a sync that no longer routes to it has been applied successfully; otherwise its address can be reused while Caddy still routes the old hostname there. Flag removal or stop paths that skip this, including in failure and cleanup branches.

Preview login keys are generated by the daemon (newLoginKey), kept per preview across redeploys, and are not secrets of ours: they may appear in the CLI output and the PR comment. Flag a login key derived from anything predictable, or reused across different previews.

Builds run only through the koi-builder BuildKit builder on the koi-build network (docker buildx build --builder). Flag a plain `docker build`, `--network host`, privileged entitlements (`--allow`), or anything that runs code from the source tree on the host.
